- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If model shows sharp upward move after a recent dip, check for mean reversion — often true price corrects downward within 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and model forecasts are rising, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid “sentiment mismatch” bias.
- Overshoots after spikes (especially >+10% from recent high) are common — cap forecast at 10% below recent peak if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If true price drops sharply after model’s peak, assume model overreacted — apply downward correction of 5–15% for 3–5 day horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true price is below 75% of 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in short-term momentum.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misjudges direction — favor 3–5 day smoothing over 30-day trend.
